explanation: Brazil has no religious or cultural rule against eating or handling food with the left hand, unlike India or parts of the Middle East where the left hand is reserved for hygiene. Brazilian table manners, rooted in European/Portuguese tradition, focus on general politeness (napkins, not reaching across the table) rather than which hand touches food.
local_tip: Eat however feels natural — using your left hand for utensils or food is not considered rude or unhygienic in Brazil.

also_check.note: The left hand is considered unclean and reserved for bathroom hygiene; food is eaten with the right hand.
Eating with the left hand is avoided under Islamic custom; the right hand is used for food.
Which hand holds chopsticks is a non-issue; left-handed eating draws no attention.
